reviewed_inputs: tasks/pipeline-queue.md (FEAT-5 round-2 note: per-table sortColumn + soft-delete filter on employee join; FEAT-7 queued next, same employeeId FK/lookup pattern)

generic_capability_vs_bespoke_route.decision: Extend the generic master-data machine (masterDataTables.js field descriptor + masterDataSchema.js + masterDataRouter.js) with two new, reusable, opt-in field-descriptor capabilities: `references` (FK-existence validation) and a new `lookupFields` table-level array (live-joined, non-stored response fields). Do NOT special-case resource_cost with its own hand-written route file.
generic_capability_vs_bespoke_route.why: FEAT-7 (queued immediately after this one) needs the identical employeeId-references-Resources + employeeName-live-lookup pattern. Building it generically once, here, means FEAT-7 consumes it via table config only — no repeated router logic, no second implementation to drift out of sync. This is a direct instance of CLAUDE.md §1 Simplicity First / Minimal Impact: one factory change serves two features instead of two bespoke code paths.

fk_existence_validation.decision: Add an optional `references: { table, column }` key to a field descriptor (e.g. `{ key: "employeeId", column: "employee_id", required: true, type: "number", references: { table: "resources", column: "employee_id" } }`). masterDataSchema.js's synchronous `validateBody` stays synchronous and unchanged (type/required checks only, as today). Add a new async `validateReferences(table, body, { partial }) ` in masterDataSchema.js (or a new masterDataReferences.js if masterDataSchema.js would otherwise grow past its current single-purpose scope — Solution Architect's call which file, not mine) that: for each field with `references` present in the request body, runs `select 1 from <ref.table> where <ref.column> = $1 and deleted_at is null`, and throws `validationError({ [field.key]: "<field.key> must reference an existing, active <ref.table> row." })` (reusing errors.js's existing 422 validation_error shape — no new error code family) if no row is found.
fk_existence_validation.constraint: Called from masterDataRouter.js's POST and PATCH handlers, after `validateBody` and before the INSERT/UPDATE, exactly the same call sites `isUniqueViolation`/`duplicateFieldError` already occupy. This keeps the 422-on-bad-FK behavior consistent with every other validation failure in the app (api.md: never return raw stack traces or a bespoke shape) and matches REQ-1's acceptance criteria (validated against `resources.employee_id`, the business key, not the `resources.id` uuid) and REQ-6 (MCP calls the same backend HTTP API, so this validation cannot be bypassed via the MCP path — do not duplicate the existence check inside mcp-server; mcp-server forwards to the backend as it already does for every table).

live_lookup_fields.decision: Add a new, separate `lookupFields` array on the table config object (sibling to `fields`, not inside it) — e.g. `lookupFields: [{ key: "employeeName", from: "resources", on: { local: "employee_id", foreign: "employee_id" }, select: "name" }, { key: "employeeDesignation", from: "resources", on: { local: "employee_id", foreign: "employee_id" }, select: "designation" }]`. These keys are never part of `fields`, so they are automatically excluded from `fields.map(f => f.column)` in POST/PATCH's INSERT/UPDATE column lists (REQ-2: never a stored/editable column) and automatically excluded from validateBody's required/type checks.
live_lookup_fields.sql_shape: masterDataRouter.js's GET list and GET-by-id queries change from `select * from ${tableName}` to a query that LEFT JOINs each `lookupFields` source table once per distinct `from` table, aliased, selecting the looked-up columns with an alias matching the lookup key's column-ish form (e.g. `r.name as employee_name, r.designation as employee_designation`), filtered with `r.deleted_at is null` on the join condition (not a WHERE, so a resource_cost row whose employee has been soft-deleted still returns the base row with employeeName/employeeDesignation coming back null rather than the whole row vanishing — this directly answers business-analyst's REQ-2 open ambiguity and is a hard constraint, matching the round-2 fix already recorded in pipeline-queue.md). `toResponse()` in masterDataSchema.js reads `table.lookupFields` the same way it reads `table.fields`, mapping each lookup key to its aliased column on the row.
live_lookup_fields.constraint: This is purely additive to the SELECT — it must not change the row shape used by INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and must not require a second query per row (one JOIN in the existing list/by-id queries, not N+1 — CLAUDE.md database.md's N+1 guidance applies even though there's no ORM here).

sort_column.decision: Confirmed and carried forward from the round-1 architecture-critic halt / round-2 fix already recorded in pipeline-queue.md: masterDataRouter.js's GET-list query must use a per-table `table.sortColumn` (falling back to `"name"` only for tables that still have a `name` column) instead of the hardcoded `order by ... name asc`. For resource_cost, set `sortColumn: "employee_id"` in masterDataTables.js. This is not optional or renegotiable at Architecture Critic (3.1) — it is already a confirmed fix from the prior halt; Solution Architect must apply it as part of this same change, not defer it.

schema_change_scope.decision: resource_cost keeps its existing `name` column untouched in this migration (business-analyst's brief and the task description do not ask for its removal — only Resources' own columns were changed in FEAT-6/migration-0012, and resource_cost's `name` column removal is out of scope here). New migration `backend/migrations/0013_add_resource_cost_columns.sql` adds only `employee_id integer` (not null — required per REQ-1), `offshore_cost numeric` (nullable), `onsite_cost numeric` (nullable), following migration 0012's exact pattern (temporary default only if backfill is needed for a NOT NULL column against existing rows, dropped immediately after; RLS/trigger conventions unchanged). No FK constraint at the DB level is required or recommended: `references` is enforced at the application/service layer per database.md and api.md ("Validate foreign keys exist at the service layer, not the route handler" — actually the service layer here IS effectively the route handler since there is no separate service layer in this codebase; the check belongs in the shared router logic added above, called from the route handler, which satisfies the intent of that rule since there is no other layer to place it in).

mcp_server_mirror.decision: mcp-server/src/masterDataTables.js's resource_cost field list must mirror the backend's field list exactly, including presence of `employeeId` as `z.number()`, required. Per the codebase-explorer's finding (no shared workspace link between backend and mcp-server field mirrors), the MCP tool description for `add_resource_cost`/`update_resource_cost` must explicitly document the FK-must-exist requirement in its Zod tool description string (contrast with modules.practiceId's existing 'optional, not validated' language) so a caller reading only the tool schema knows this differs from the unvalidated-FK precedent. The MCP tool itself performs no independent existence check — it forwards to the backend HTTP API via apiClient.js exactly as today, so the single point of enforcement is the backend router change above (Security by Default: validate at the boundary, and there is exactly one real boundary here).

scaling_and_complexity_risks: Risk: `lookupFields` becomes a second, informally-specified mini-ORM if its shape isn't nailed down before Solution Architect designs the SDD. Mitigation: this stage fixes the exact shape (`from`, `on: {local, foreign}`, `select`) so System Engineer/Developer implement one agreed contract, not three different interpretations across FEAT-5 and FEAT-7.

Risk: adding a JOIN to the shared GET query for every table, even ones with no lookupFields, could regress performance or query-building complexity for the other seven tables. Mitigation: the JOIN clause must be built conditionally — only tables whose config actually defines `lookupFields` get extra JOIN clauses in the generated SQL; tables with no lookupFields keep the exact `select * from ${tableName}` shape they have today, unchanged.

Risk: FEAT-5 and FEAT-7 both touch masterDataRouter.js/masterDataTables.js/masterDataSchema.js concurrently — pipeline-queue.md already records the owner's decision to run FEAT-7 only after FEAT-5 settles rather than truly in parallel, specifically to avoid one clobbering the other's edits to these shared files. This tech-lead direction reinforces why that sequencing decision is correct: FEAT-7 should be built on top of the generic `references`/`lookupFields` capability this feature introduces, not as a second parallel implementation of the same idea.

Risk: a soft-deleted Resources row silently returning null employeeName/employeeDesignation could look like a data-integrity bug to a future reader rather than an intentional soft-delete behavior. Mitigation: the LEFT JOIN's `deleted_at is null` condition and its rationale must be documented with a short WHY comment at the query site, per CLAUDE.md §1 (comment the non-obvious why, not the what).
hard_constraints_for_solution_architect: FK-existence validation is a new generic `references: { table, column }` field-descriptor capability plus an async `validateReferences` check called from the shared router's POST/PATCH — not a resource_cost-specific route file.

Live-lookup fields are a new generic table-level `lookupFields` array (never inside `fields`), rendered via a conditional LEFT JOIN added to the shared GET list/by-id queries only for tables that declare them — never a per-row second query (no N+1).

The LEFT JOIN's soft-delete filter (`deleted_at is null`) lives on the join condition, not a WHERE clause, so a resource_cost row survives in output even if its referenced Resources row is later soft-deleted; employeeName/employeeDesignation become null in that case rather than the row disappearing.
resource_cost's GET-list query uses an explicit `sortColumn: "employee_id"` from table config, not the hardcoded `name` column — carrying forward the already-confirmed round-1/round-2 fix.

resource_cost's existing `name` column is left untouched by this migration; only employee_id (required), offshore_cost (optional), onsite_cost (optional) are added, following migration 0012's pattern exactly (temporary defaults dropped immediately, RLS/trigger conventions preserved).

No DB-level FOREIGN KEY constraint on resource_cost.employee_id — validation is enforced at the application layer (the shared router), consistent with there being no separate service layer in this codebase.

MCP server's employeeId parameter is `z.number()`, required, with a tool description explicitly stating the FK-must-exist requirement (contrast with modules.practiceId's 'not validated' language); MCP performs no independent validation of its own — it forwards to the backend API, which is the single enforcement point.

Frontend column labels for resource-cost: "Employee ID", "Employee Name", "Employee Designation", "Offshore Cost", "Onsite Cost", ordered before the audit columns, matching FEAT-6's Resources labeling convention exactly.

This generic `references`/`lookupFields` capability must be built so FEAT-7 (queued next) can reuse it for its own employeeId FK + employeeName lookup without re-implementing router logic — FEAT-7's positionId/positionName stay plain, unvalidated, non-lookup fields for now (no Positions table exists), matching the existing modules.practiceId unvalidated-FK precedent.
open_items_deferred_to_solution_architec: Exact file location for the new `validateReferences` function and `lookupFields` JOIN-building logic (extend masterDataSchema.js/masterDataRouter.js in place, or split into a new small module) — an implementation-organization call, not an architecture-blocking one, as long as the generic-capability-not-bespoke-route constraint holds.

Whether a temporary default value is needed on `employee_id` during migration 0013 depends on whether resource_cost currently has existing rows — System Engineer/Database Specialist to check live data before writing the migration, per the 0012 precedent's own note that it only needed defaults because the table was empty at the time.
verdict_notes: No architectural objection to proceeding. This stage resolves both open architecture questions the codebase-explorer and business-analyst correctly flagged as undecided (how FK-existence validation and computed/joined fields should be expressed generically) by committing to two small, additive, opt-in extensions to the existing declarative master-data machine, rather than a one-off resource_cost route. This keeps the three invariants in CLAUDE.md §7.6 intact (code accumulates forward onto the existing factory, no forbidden bespoke duplication) and directly sets up FEAT-7 to reuse the same mechanism. The already-confirmed sortColumn fix from the round-1/round-2 halt is carried forward as a non-negotiable constraint so it isn't accidentally dropped between pipeline stages.
summary: Set concrete architecture direction for FEAT-5's Resource Cost real-schema build: extend the shared master-data machine (masterDataTables.js/masterDataSchema.js/masterDataRouter.js) with two new generic, opt-in field-descriptor capabilities instead of a bespoke resource_cost route — (1) `references: { table, column }` on a field descriptor plus a new async `validateReferences` check called from the shared router's POST/PATCH, enforcing employeeId's existence against resources.employee_id and returning the existing 422 validation_error shape on failure; and (2) a new table-level `lookupFields` array driving a conditional LEFT JOIN in the shared GET queries (soft-delete-safe via the join condition, not a WHERE) to produce non-stored, always-current employeeName/employeeDesignation. Also carried forward the already-confirmed sortColumn fix (per-table sort key instead of hardcoded `name`) and confirmed migration 0013 only adds employee_id/offshore_cost/onsite_cost, leaving resource_cost's existing name column untouched, with no DB-level FK constraint (app-layer validation only, no separate service layer exists in this codebase). MCP server mirrors employeeId as a required z.number() with an explicit FK-must-exist tool description, forwarding to the backend for the actual check. Listed eight hard constraints for the Solution Architect stage, four scaling/complexity risks with mitigations, and explicitly designed this as reusable by the next-queued FEAT-7 (same employeeId pattern) to avoid two independent implementations of the same capability. Verdict PASS — no blocking findings; this is a read-only architecture-direction stage, no application code was created or edited.
